author: m.kalinin
content: Now it's getting clearer to me. So, we have `N` blocks behind the most recent finalized checkpoint, for the period of non-finality this implies also retaining blocks up until the head after that checkpoint

author: m.kalinin
content: There were efforts on supporting the checkpoint sync from a non-finalized checkpoint in several clients, not sure about that status of this work. This is helpful for bootstrapping a node during long non-finality period or for switching a node to a desirable fork. Starting from a finalized checkpoint in this case may also work. If EL has been bootstrapped already and the restart happens with wiping out CL's database leaving EL with the state it has, then EL will be syncing by executing blocks from the point where it went offline and it will be helpful to have those blocks in the network, otherwise, EL will need to get wiped out and snap synced from scratch i guess

content: i.e. this is one advantage of having a method to treat the EL as a kind of library which doesn't itself need to gossip

author: m.kalinin
content: top-up sync relies on blocks requested over p2p, right? So, beacon blocks and payloads should be available since the point in time when node went offline
